blocks.text: If you only have time for one, come at sunrise. Bondi faces almost due east onto the Pacific, so the sun climbs straight out of the ocean here — the best light show the beach gives you all day. Sunset is a quieter, sneakier pleasure: the sun drops behind the suburbs at your back, but the sky and the sandstone cliffs catch a soft pink glow I love just as much. Here are my favourite spots for both, and how to time them.

blocks.text: The whole eastern edge of Bondi is a front-row seat, but a few spots lift it from lovely to unforgettable.

This is my desert-island pick. From the clifftop lookout at the southern end of the beach — the first headland on the Bondi to Bronte walk — you look back across the whole arc of sand with the sun coming up over the water beyond Ben Buckler. The sandstone catches the first light beautifully, and roughly between May and November you've a genuine chance of spotting migrating whales offshore while you wait.
Bondi Icebergs and the south corner

You don't need to be swimming to get the shot every visitor wants: the ocean pool in the foreground, waves washing over its edge, sky on fire behind. Stand on the promenade above the pool at the south end of the beach. If you want to swim laps at first light, check the Icebergs website for current pool session times first — they change seasonally and the pool shuts for cleaning.

The northern end is calmer and less photographed. The rocks below the North Bondi headland and around Ben Buckler give you crashing surf in the foreground and an open eastern horizon — a peaceful alternative when the south corner is busy.

Check the exact sunrise time the night before (Geoscience Australia's sun times tool is spot-on for Sydney) and arrive 30–40 minutes early. The richest colour — the 'blue hour' and first pink — comes well before the sun clears the horizon, and the best clifftop parking fills fast on clear mornings.

Here's what nobody tells you: you won't see the sun sink into the sea at Bondi, because it sets behind the land to the west. So chase the afterglow instead. As the sun drops at your back, the eastern sky over the ocean turns soft lilac and rose, and the cliffs and the pale Icebergs building light up gold. Marks Park, on the grassy clifftop just past Mackenzies Point, is my go-to — spread a picnic, face the sea, and watch the colour deepen.

blocks.title: For actual sunset-over-water
blocks.text: If watching the sun drop into the horizon is the whole point for you, Sydney's west-facing harbour spots do it far better than any east-coast beach. At Bondi, come for the sunrise and stay for the afterglow — that's what this coastline does best.

blocks.title: Mind the edge
blocks.text: The clifftop lookouts are unfenced in places and the rock platforms below can be hit by sudden waves. Stay back from wet rock and the edge in low light, and never turn your back on the surf for a photo.

items.q: Can you watch the sun set over the ocean at Bondi Beach?
items.a: No — Bondi faces east, so the sun rises over the water and sets behind the suburbs to the west. Come at sunrise for the sun-over-ocean show; at sunset, watch the pink afterglow light up the eastern sky and the cliffs instead.

items.q: What's the best spot for sunrise at Bondi?
items.a: My pick is Mackenzies Point, the south headland at the start of the Bondi to Bronte walk, for the view back across the whole beach. The promenade above Bondi Icebergs is best for the classic ocean-pool-and-sky photo.

items.q: What time is sunrise and sunset at Bondi?
items.a: It shifts through the year — sunrise ranges from roughly 5:40am in midsummer to about 7am in winter. Check Geoscience Australia's sun times tool for the exact time on your date rather than guessing.

items.q: Might I see whales while watching the sunrise?
items.a: Possibly, roughly between May and November during the humpback migration. Mackenzies Point is one of the better clifftop vantage points — bring binoculars and scan the horizon.

items.q: Do I need to pay or book?
items.a: No. Every spot here is free public headland or promenade. The only thing worth checking ahead is Bondi Icebergs' pool session times if you plan to swim, as those change seasonally.

blocks.text: Whichever end you choose, put your phone down for the last few minutes. There's a particular hush at Bondi just as the sky turns — joggers slow, surfers sit up on their boards, and the whole beach seems to hold its breath. That's the bit you'll remember.
